commentary: In the first quarter, the fund printed a stellar return although it trailed its benchmark the Bloomberg Commodity Index.  The strategy started the year on a strong note and posted positive returns in all 3 months.  However, March was an outlier as the index posted its best month since 2009.  This was primarily thanks to the Energy complex, which returned +40%, its best monthly performance since 1986.  These moves highlight the magnitude of the stress caused by the Iran conflict which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and consequently sent the oil price close to 50% higher.  Precious metals were the laggard with the BCOM Gold Index down -11.5%, Silver -19.7%, Platinum -18% and Palladium -18.6%.  This was the worst monthly sell-off since the 2008 GFC.  Industrial metals posted mixed returns as Aluminium rose +11.5% while Copper fell -7.4%.  Grain reacted strongly to the conflict although in a volatile way, Soybean Oil gained +10.8% whereas Soybean Meal lost -1.3%. Softs gained +9.3%, all 4 commodities registered gains, led by Cocoa (+14.3%), followed by Sugar (+11.7%), Cotton (+6.7%) and Coffee (+6.3%).  Livestocks printed mixed returns, Feeder Cattle and Live cattle increased +5.6% and +5.9% respectively while Lean Hogs declined -4.8%.  In this context, the fund benefited from its overweight Gasoil (+1.27%) and soybean Oil (+0.24%) as well as from its underweight Silver (+0.16%).  Reversely, weak contract selection in Crude Oil detracted -1.37% (essentially in the 1st week of March), followed by the overweight Gold (-0.8%) and the underweight Coffee (-0.35%).  The fund entered the month of March with a strong allocation in longer-dated contracts in the Energy sector.  They quickly acted as this conflict will not be a short-lived one and started to overwrite these carry trades across the whole energy complex and to overweight brent and gasoil over the course of the first week of March. They started to take profit on the beneficial long position in gasoil in the last few days of March.  They maintained their bearish positioning on US Natural Gas.  They stayed overweight Gold, in light of what they believe will be a prolonged conflict.  They implemented an underweight Silver which they closed at month end.  They maintained their underweight Industrial Metals, especially in Zinc and Copper.  At the same time, they established an overweight Aluminium.  They closed their underweight in Grains, especially in Wheat and Corn as the fertilizer crisis and higher energy prices increase input costs.  They took profit in their Coffee underweight and established an overweight Sugar.  They closed the overweight Cattle and the off-benchmark position in EU Carbon allowance.  At quarter end, the largest exposure is Crude Oil (24.5%), followed by Gold (19%), Gasoil (7.8%), Aluminum (7%), Soybean Oil (6.4%) and Corn (5.7%).  In relative terms, the largest underweight are Copper (-3.2%), Zinc (-2.3%), Soybean Meal (-1.7%), Soybeans (-0.9%) and Silver (-0.5%). Reversely, the main overweight are Gold (+6.1%), Crude Oil (+3.4%), Aluminum (+3.3%), Soybean Oil (+3.1%) and Gasoil (+2.8%). Among sectors, the fund is overweight energy (46.7% vs 39%), Precious Metals (22% vs 16.1%), Grains (21.2% vs 19.8%) and Softs (7.6% vs 6.7%).  It is underweight Industrial Metals (10.9% vs 13.2%), and neutral Livestocks (2.1%).  The overall exposure stands at 113.6% versus 104.8% at the end of Q4 2025.
